newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to free 25 more wrongly jailed for terrorism.
newsitem.headline: Peru to free 25 more wrongly jailed for terrorism.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori said on Monday that Peru would release another 25 prisoners wrongly jailed on terrorism charges early next month.

He said the 25 would be the first to benefit from pardons recommended by a special government commission created in August to investigate the hundreds of Peruvians believed to be falsely convicted of guerrilla activities. The releases would bring to 210 the total of innocent prisoners released since the beginning of 1995.

"Achieving the freedom of these citizens was a titanic task and, at the same time, gratifying for those of us who believe in justice," Fujimori said at a ceremony to inaugurate the new office of the nation's ombudsman.

The government has said that up to 400 prisoners may remain in jail on false terrorism charges but local human rights groups put the number as high as 1,000. Most were convicted by Peru's controversial "faceless" court system, introduced by Fujimori in mid-1992 to combat then-escalating guerrilla violence from the Maoist Shining Path and the smaller Cuban-styled Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement.

Rights groups say many were jailed by these secret courts on flimsy evidence, often obtained under torture, and without the possibility of a fair defence. The "faceless" tribunals, whose anonymous judges usually wear hoods when passing sentence, are due to end their functions on Oct. 15.
Peru's guerrilla conflicts have cost at least 30,000 lives and $25 billion in infrastructure damage since 1980.
